title: Make the Exorcist Fall in Love
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: A priest raised by the Catholic Church from birth to fight demons, so literal in his faith that he tore out his own eye to resist the demon of lust, is assigned to guard the artist Imuri Atsuki from Satan's agents. Imuri is secretly a succubus sent by Satan to make him fall in love. Their romance unfolds amid a bloody holy war between Church and demons.
life_message: A person is more than the weapon an institution makes of them; love and gentle desires are worth defending.

content.note: Bloody battles with demons (AniList Gore tag, rank 77; publisher blurb 'bloody holy war'); priest's self-inflicted eye injury (Wikipedia).
Tragedy and demonic horror (AniList Tragedy and Demons tags; Wikipedia premise).
Succubus seduction plot (Wikipedia); AniList Succubus and spoiler Psychosexual tags; MangaDex suggestive. Some boys' love elements (AniList, to verify).
Priest tears out his own eye; mentor calls him too self-sacrificial (Wikipedia); depth to verify.
Literal self-mutilation for faith presented as a wound to heal, not a model.

Dignity vs honor.evidence: Holy war against demons framed as duty more than personal vengeance.

Order vs freedom.evidence: Church discipline governs the priest, and the story questions it.

Civic vs kin.evidence: Institutional loyalty to the Church, not family, defines the hero.

Equality vs hierarchy.evidence: Clerical hierarchy and Satan's command structure on both sides.

Tradition vs secular-rational.evidence: Religious framework taken seriously yet critiqued.

Survival vs self-expression.evidence: The priest's wish to bake sweets and love stands against his assigned survival role.

folkways.japan: Western Christian institutions are reimagined through a Japanese fantasy lens, common in manga where the Church serves as exotic setting rather than lived faith.
